catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albenga: A 1913 entry on Albenga — the Ligurian diocese of the Riviera. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its baptistery is a fifth-century gem. Bishops watched the Genoese sea. An ancient see on the Italian shore. Its towers guard the old seaport.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-albrec: This 1913 reference article on Albert of Riga — the apostle of Livonia. F.M. Rudge tells his missionary wars. He founded Riga in 1201. The Sword Brothers carried his cross. The Baltic's Christianizer. His cathedral still crowns the old town. His sword-brothers guarded the mission frontier.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alonso-de-erc: This 1913 reference piece on Alonso de Ercilla — the soldier-poet of La Araucana. Ventura Fuentes honors his epic. He sang Chile's wars from the saddle. The Araucanians found their Homer. Spain's noblest epic of the New World. His stanzas were written on campaign.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alpha-and-ome: A 1913 entry on Alpha and Omega in Christian art — the letters on tombs and mosaics. Christian Van den Biesen gathers the monuments. The catacombs carved them in stone. Christ's eternity, pictured simply. Art's oldest monogram. Their monogram seals the Christian graves.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andreas-de-ve: This 1913 reference article on Andreas de Vega — the Franciscan theologian of Trent. Michael Bihl honors his learning. His pen defended justification's truth. The council heard his voice. A friar among the doctors. His De justificatione defended the council. His order honors its theologian.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-astorga: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Astorga — the Spanish diocese of the Maragato land. The entry gives its ancient story. Its bishops date from Roman times. Gaudí's palace crowns the old town. A see of the Leonese plain. Its walls guard the pilgrim road.
